stories.name: Rep. Thomas Massie files articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
facts: On Monday, Nov. 9, Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) introduced and read on the House floor a resolution with eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, then discussed it at a news conference on Capitol Hill.
The articles focus mainly on waging the war with Iran without congressional authorization, and also cite the Caribbean boat strikes and the Pentagon's scrutiny of Sen. Mark Kelly.

Impeachment resolutions are privileged, so House leaders must act (table, refer or vote) within two legislative days. Speaker Mike Johnson opposed it; Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries supports it; Hegseth called the effort a sham and scheduled a Tuesday news conference.

people.name: Thomas Massie
people.verified_action: Read the articles of impeachment on the House floor on Nov. 9 (CBS News, CNBC). Drawn standing at a House floor lectern holding the resolution pages and speaking; slim build, glasses, short grey hair, dark suit; no text.

people.name: Pete Hegseth
people.verified_action: Subject of the resolution; said he was not worried and called it a sham (CBS News, CNBC). Not drawn as a figure.

stories.visual_notes: Low angle up at Massie at a floor lectern in the House chamber: rows of curved seats, the Speaker's rostrum tiers and the large US flag behind it. The resolution's eight pages lift and spiral up into the skylit ceiling as a symbolic motif (illustration, not a claim). Clerks at the rostrum and a few members seated, neutral. No text, no Hegseth figure, no vote outcome.
stories.confidence: high: CBS News and CNBC (both read in full, independent reporting) agree that Massie introduced eight articles on the House floor on Nov. 9 and on the two-legislative-day timing; NYT, NPR, Globe and others carry the same headline.
